regime_context: The detector shows Big Banks as the headline trend with a true absolute-trend gate flag (eligible, durability_bar 0.8, breadth 1.0, not crowded), while the top-ranked theme Oil & Gas Producers is NOT eligible (gate fails, mixed trend, durability 0.19) — so the rank order is mostly an attention lens, not a tradable hierarchy. Breadth of eligible themes is narrowing (7 of 16, frac 0.44) and rotation is non-directional, consistent with a defensive, trend-discipline-on regime.
emerging_watch: Watching Oil & Gas Producers (XEG.TO) to see if the absolute-trend gate flips to eligible=true AND durability_bar recovers above ~0.5; while it leads the momentum rank, it remains trend-gate ineligible and would need that confirmed flip plus breadth >0.5 before I would treat it as a handoff candidate rather than a fading rank leader.

theses.subject: Big Banks
theses.thesis: Big Banks is the only theme combining the absolute-trend gate (eligible=true) with strong trend health (durability_bar 0.8, hurst_tag trend), full internal breadth (1.0), and a neutral crowding profile. The validated edge in this market is drawdown/shake-out avoidance via the trend gate, and Big Banks is the eligible leader. The momentum rank is not a return forecast, but the gate + durability legs support staying-power exposure.
theses.dissent: The directional accuracy of this analyst's past calls is only 0.313 over 147 calls, so even a well-gated trend is no return edge — Big Banks has been the consensus trade and mean reversion in financials could compress returns relative to the broad TSX.

theses.subject: Consumer Staples & Retail
theses.thesis: The theme passes the trend gate (eligible) and has high durability (0.79) and full breadth (1.0), but it is the only eligible theme flagged crowded (crowded=true, crowding_z 1.03). Crowding is a size-down caution only — never a fade — but combined with the narrowing eligible set it argues for not adding exposure here while the defensive trend remains intact.
theses.dissent: In a defensive regime, crowded staples may be exactly where trend-followers should stay — crowding flags have no basket-level forward edge and capping exposure too aggressively could leave a trend on the table.

falsifier.text: XST.TO outperforms the S&P/TSX by 4% over the next 30 trading days while remaining above its 200-day average
